title: The Ophiuchus DIsk Survey Employing ALMA (ODISEA): Disk Dust Mass Distributions across Protostellar Evolutionary Classes
question: How do disk dust mass distributions vary across protostellar infrared classes (I, Flat, II, III) in Ophiuchus, and how do Class II masses compare with other regions?

what.value: Lupus and Upper Scorpius ALMA flux densities, ages and distances for comparison

evidence.quote: Disk masses were recalculated from the observed flux densities with the same uniform temperature and opacity prescription

what.value: Sample A ALMA observations and sample selection

evidence.quote: Paper I describes the full sample selection and the observations of sample A

recipe.method: Point-source fit to visibilities with uvmodelfit; aperture photometry for binary and resolved sources
Gaia DR2 parallax inversion; mean distance otherwise; remove background (pi<2.5 mas) and misclassified sources
Optically thin M = F d^2/(kappa B(T))
key_parameters: detection if flux >= 3 rms and position within 1'' of Spitzer position; upper limits at 3 rms
assumptions: T_dust = 20 K, kappa_nu = (nu/100 GHz) cm^2/g, optically thin

recipe.goal: Derive cumulative mass distributions and log-normal fits per class and region
recipe.method: Survival analysis for upper limits; gaussian in log mass fitted to cumulative distributions
key_parameters: Region comparison restricted to J-band <= 12 mag (masses >~0.2 Msun)

answer_key.quantity: Upper Sco Class II mean mass

evidence.quote: final sample of 265 sources (279 disks after allowing for 12 binaries and one triple system)

not_stated_but_needed: tclean parameters (weighting, robust, cell, image size, deconvolver, masking)
Survival analysis implementation and gaussian fitting method/priors
Sample A fluxes (from Paper I) used in the class comparison
Exact J-band source selection and the Lupus/Upper Sco flux tables used
missing_for_reproduction: Sample A flux values from Paper I
Survival analysis and fitting code details
score_reason: Data public and the mass formula is explicit, but imaging and fitting details are missing and sample A comes from Paper I.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple numeric recipe (flux to mass, log-normal fit) and numeric results, though some imaging details are absent.
